messages.author: cd79aec8f4be0778
messages.subject: Hessian Warnings
parts:
Dear all,

I am doing a little sophisticated "bym" model and I get these warnings:


*** WARNING *** Eigenvalue 2 of the Hessian is -0.183833 < 0
*** WARNING *** Set this eigenvalue to 2.03328
*** WARNING *** This have consequence for the accurancy of
*** WARNING *** the approximations; please check!!!
*** WARNING *** R-inla: Use option inla(..., control.inla = list(h = h.value), ...)
*** WARNING *** R-inla: to chose a different `h.value'.

I think that I have a problem with the numerical computation of the Hessian. I have tried changing the option (with h = 0.001) and changing the initials but I obtain the same warnings.

Can anyone help me? I don't now which criteria I should consider to change the values of "h". Should the value be increased or decreased?

Thank you very much!

Marc

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: Hessian Warnings
parts:
Hi Marc,

I'm not 100% on what's gone wrong (more of Håvard's area and he'll probably step in if I'm too wrong!), but I can explain the process and point out where it may have gone wrong.

In essence, this bit of INLA does the following:

1) Find the mode of the Laplace approximation posterior \pi(\theta|y)
2) Compute the Hessian at the mode (not computed during the optimization!)
3) Do stuff with the Hessian

Something can go wrong at the first two stages.  The optimizer may stop before it reaches the mode, which will result in the Hessian not necessarily being positive definite.  You can try to fix this by playing with the parameters of the optimization routine (try the tolerance and restart options in control.inla).

The other thing that can go wrong is that the approximate Hessian, which is computed by Finite Differences, is not sufficiently accurate.  This is changed by playing with the h parameter.

Another option is to just "help the optimizer along" by having a pilot run on an easier (but different!) model.  This is explained here: http://www.r-inla.org/?place=msg%2Fr-inla-discussion-group%2Fuf2ZGh4jmWc%2FA0rdPE5W7uMJ

Hope this helps,

Dan

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Hessian Warnings
parts:
On Tue, 2013-07-23 at 02:51 -0700, Alex wrote:
>
> Hello,
>
> I would like to ask if this Hessian warning is extractable from an
> inla() object? (rather than looking it from the console)
>
> The purpose would be to put a condition on that, and start a loop of
> diagonal,tolerance,restart arguments...

I presume you mean if the Hessian is not pos def?
if so then result$mode$mode.status > 0, the higher the worse

result = inla.rerun(result)

might help.

but $mode.status picks up other things as well, so maybe we have to be
more spesific.

you can always check in the logfile

result$logfile

and 'grep' for the hessian and check in this way.

let me know if we need to add something else.

H

--
Håvard Rue
he...@r-inla.org
